**Finding 1 (high, correctness — unit-wide disclaimer suppression):** `scan_text()` no longer skips a whole unit when any disclaimer appears. Units that make an executor claim are now split into clauses at semicolons and sentence ends (`_CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE` in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/doc_drift.py:73`), and an agent is excused only when *every* clause naming it carries a disclaimer. Clauses deliberately do not split on commas or dashes: commas would break "Gemini, Grok, Ollama executors" as one claim list, and dashes would false-positive on README's honest em-dash apposition at line 29 ("**Operator-only runtimes** — Gemini and Grok today — … cannot be dispatched as workers"). The auditor's exact probe `Gemini is a shipped executor; Grok is operator-only` now flags gemini, covered by the parametrized regression `test_disclaimer_for_one_agent_does_not_excuse_another` (semicolon and sentence-boundary variants) plus `test_em_dash_apposition_disclaimer_still_counts` guarding the no-dash-split decision.

**Finding 2 (medium, test_coverage — tests contradict registry-driven relaxation):** Added `HISTORICAL_REGISTRY = frozenset({"claude", "codex"})` (the registry as of the drift incident) and injected it into every historical-fixture test — pre-F001 checklist, bare prose claim, corrected phrasing, mixed-claim probes, and the tmp-path allowlist test — so legitima
